Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we prepare the activation MAP for CompassRx, leadership wants explicit calibration on performance acceptance: we need TTFT and streaming latency targets (p50/p95/p99), sustained concurrency guidance, and a suggested canary/close timeline so procurement can align.

Key asks:
- TTFT (first-token latency) targets for the chat endpoint, by model variant.
- Streaming latency (p50/p95/p99) with token streaming enabled.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and recommended autoscale settings for 100/500/1k concurrent sessions.
- Any known caveats (cold KV cache, prefix caching, quantized model differences).

Can you send a short MAP addendum with the evaluation plan and a proposed close date? We’re targeting a production cutover in Q3 and would like to lock dates this month.

Regards,

Emma — thanks, great to align. Draft MAP addendum attached (MAP-activation-performance-signal.xlsx). Below is a concise evaluation plan and the performance signal we propose for acceptance.

Evaluation plan (high level):
1) Test harness: synthetic chat workload that mimics 1–3 message turns (user prompt + 1 assistant token stream). Warmup run -> 30m sustained window -> spike tests.
2) Variants: redwood-instruct-13B-fp16 (high quality), redwood-open-7B-q4 (cost-optimized).
3) Metrics:
   - TTFT: measured from request receipt (server-side) to first token sent to client.
   - Streaming latencies: p50/p95/p99 measured per token emission during first 20 tokens.
   - Throughput: tokens/sec aggregated at the model route level during sustained window.
4) Concurrency targets: test at 100 / 500 / 1,000 concurrent sessions with a realistic think-time distribution (exp mean 12s).
5) Failure modes capture: cold KV cache, model swap fallback, autoscale ramp delay.

Acceptance signal (proposed):
- redwood-instruct-13B-fp16 (baseline)
  - TTFT p50 <= 160ms, p95 <= 320ms, p99 <= 650ms
  - Streaming token emission (first 20 tokens) p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 260ms
  - Sustained throughput: >= 6,500 tokens/sec at 500 concurrent sessions
- redwood-open-7B-q4 (cost-optimized)
  - TTFT p50 <= 220ms, p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 800ms
  - Streaming emission p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 160ms, p99 <= 340ms
  - Sustained throughput: >= 11,000 tokens/sec at 500 concurrent sessions

Notes: TTFT targets assume prefix caching enabled and a warmed KV cache. Cold-start p99 spikes are expected and will be marked as excluded from the steady-state acceptance window if we see evidence of system coldness during the test window.

Proposed timeline (MAP milestones):
- 06/18: Redwood delivers benchmark run + raw logs (attached: ttft-streaming-p50p95p99.csv, streaming-test-logs.txt)
- 06/22: Customer validation window starts (3 business days)
- 06/28: Canary deployment (10% traffic)
- 07/02: Final sign-off / procurement close

I attached the spreadsheet with the formal MAP and the raw CSV. Please let me know if you want the tests re-run with a different concurrency mix.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Subject: Re: Activation MAP & perf acceptance criteria — benchmark results

Emma / Sean — ran the benchmark on a dedicated G5 pool (4xA100-equivalent nodes) with prefix caching enabled. Summary here; raw CSV and logs attached.

Summary (steady-state window, 30m):
- redwood-instruct-13B-fp16:
  - TTFT: p50=148ms, p95=305ms, p99=610ms
  - Streaming (first 20 tokens): p50=42ms, p95=110ms, p99=240ms
  - Sustained throughput @500 concurrent: 6,750 tokens/sec
- redwood-open-7B-q4:
  - TTFT: p50=205ms, p95=395ms, p99=780ms
  - Streaming: p50=58ms, p95=150ms, p99=330ms
  - Sustained throughput @500 concurrent: 11,450 tokens/sec

Observations:
- We saw an intermittent p99 bump for the 13B run (~3 samples in the 30m window) correlated with KV cache thrash during a simulated model-swap. Those spikes are visible in streaming-test-logs.txt lines 1,482–1,518.
- When we pre-warmed the KV cache for 15 minutes before the steady-state window, p99 improved by ~10–12% across the board.
- Quantized 7B shows more steady throughput but slightly higher TTFT variance on tail due to quantized kernel latency jitter under heavy batching.

Recommendation: exclude initial 5 minutes of the run from acceptance aggregation, and require pre-warm step in the MAP checklist. Also recommend enabling small autoscale headroom to avoid model-swap induced KV thrash during ramp.

Next actions:
- Sean: circulate the CSV to CompassRx stakeholders (done).
- Marissa: update MAP timelines to add pre-warm task and operator owner.
- Connor/Karthik: prepare canary deployment recipe for 06/28.

-Vanessa
Sr. Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — that looks promising and within the ballpark of our internal SLOs. Couple of clarifying Qs:

1) For the 1,000 concurrent sessions run, do you have the throughput numbers? We need to confirm vertical scaling behavior.
2) What’s the recommended autoscale buffer (percent over observed throughput) to keep p95 < target during sudden burst?

If we can get a short note on those two items, procurement is comfortable moving the signature forward pending canary success.

Emma

Emma — quick follow-up with the 1k results and recommended autoscale buffer.

1k concurrent (sustained 20m window):
- redwood-instruct-13B-fp16: throughput ~12,800 tokens/sec, TTFT p95 ~360ms (p99 ~720ms)
- redwood-open-7B-q4: throughput ~21,400 tokens/sec, TTFT p95 ~440ms (p99 ~860ms)

Recommended autoscale buffer: 25% headroom over observed peak throughput for the canary phase. That keeps p95 comfortably under the acceptance threshold during typical bursts (our stress runs show 18–23% variance).
